# NOTIFY150_R1: direct Lua150 notification fix

This build targets the crash in both BASELINE150_R1 dumps. The native notification
callback had room for only 50 IDs and copied from a 50-ID inline source. The new
build gives that callback room for 150 IDs and supplies the matching full request
sidecar. Increasing the frame alone would still send incorrect IDs after ID50.

The ASI is staged here, not installed or live-tested. All other capacities remain
unchanged: 150 requests /160 graphics slots, ED/EF sidecars, indexed262144,
resource collection131072, cleanup262144, pending512, audio models192,
global audio slots2048, shared default audio64MiB, callback512.

## First test: repeat the failing request

1. Close the game. Replace the enabled traffic ASI with
   `DriverSF_V29s_160Capacity_150Request_NOTIFY150_R1.asi`.
   Enable exactly one traffic ASI. Keep ARENA_REUSE_R1 outside the plugin
   directory for rollback to the previously tested normal-transition workload.
2. Keep the original `san_franciscoAI.fchunk` used in the two failing runs.
   An initial named roster of18 with `assetMismatch` is expected under the
   existing asset guard; it does not invalidate this direct Lua test.
3. Start a fresh process, load the same save normally, and allow loading to finish.
   The log is `%TEMP%\DSFV29s_notify150_<PID>.log`. Require both
   `DSFV29s_BASELINE_START revision=1 status=1` and
   `DSFV29s_NOTIFY150_START revision=1 status=1 patches=5`.
4. Run the contents of `NOTIFY150_R1_LUA_TEST.lua` in your existing Lua tool.
   It only defines helpers. Then call:

   ```lua
   DSF150Baseline.status()
   DSF150Baseline.request()
   ```

   Issue the request once. If the helper reports busy, wait for the transition
   to finish before retrying. Do not use this helper on the older ASIs.
5. Check that the command returns and the game continues. The new copy record
   should contain `count=150 storage=sidecar rosterHash=5CBDFFEA first=62 last=303`.
   Wait10–20 seconds, then call `DSF150Baseline.status()` again.
6. Drive briefly and report rendering, engine/tire/horn audio, rough FPS and how
   the run ended. Copy the new log into `dist/MAIN_150`. First establish whether
   the reported crash is resolved; longer Challenge/menu/reload checks follow.

The direct request changes the resource roster, not the original civilian
selection weights. It does not make all150 cars appear in ordinary traffic.
A subsequent named setting can replace the requested roster.

## Checks and scope

`NOTIFY150_STATUS` reports inline/sidecar copies, peak count and invalid copies.
Startup or source-invariant failure writes `NOTIFY150_FATAL` and terminates with
code0x29F2 rather than continuing with an unsafe notification. Such a run fails.
Preserve that log if it occurs.

The complete native callback, event writer, ring writer and replay dispatcher
passed isolated tests, including all counts0–150, ring wrap and a150-ID event
round trip. External factory/timestamp/request services were stubbed. This is
not a live game result. A separate fixed-size full traffic snapshot format
remains unexpanded; Film Director/full snapshot support is not certified.

Inherited readiness sweeps and body-draw CALL observations remain enabled.
Request counts, native READY and draw calls do not prove visible pixels or
audible playback. A phase with zero checkpoints is unmeasured. Some roster IDs
are trailers/special vehicles without ordinary engine/horn behavior.

Analyze a supplied log with both tools:

```powershell
python scripts/analyze_baseline150_log.py dist/MAIN_150/DSFV29s_notify150_PID.log --output analysis/notify150_PID/coverage.json
python scripts/analyze_callback_log.py dist/MAIN_150/DSFV29s_notify150_PID.log --output analysis/notify150_PID/inherited.json
```

The first analyzer also checks notification startup, failures and the observed
150-ID sidecar copy. Neither analyzer certifies the150-car baseline by itself.
